awarded_note: No cumulative drawdown figure is published. Individual awards are visible as they occur — e.g. the £65.5m Viking development-fund grant in July 2026 (corpus record 2026-07-16#01) — but these are drawdown against the programme, not additional money.
quote: the UK government announced up to £21.7 billion pounds of funding support over the next 25 years for two CCS clusters
note: The single largest CCS funding commitment by any government in this register. At £21.7bn over 25 years the simple average is ~£870m a year, but the profile is not flat — early years are construction-heavy. Treat the annual average as an ordering aid, not a budget line.

quote: a £960 million fund for CCUS, greenhouse gas removals (GGRs), and hydrogen
note: Shared across CCUS, greenhouse-gas removal and hydrogen — the CCS share is not broken out.

awarded_note: Nearly US$2.2bn awarded or in award negotiations as at June 2024 — about 18% of the appropriation.
quote: Nearly US$2.2 billion of the BIL’s US$12.5 billion appropriations for carbon management have been awarded or are in negotiations
note: The clearest published example of the gap between a headline appropriation and money actually moving: roughly four-fifths of this pot was still unawarded nearly three years after the law passed.

awarded_note: Up to US$1.2bn selected for two hubs (Louisiana and Texas), each targeting 1 Mtpa.
quote: two DAC hubs, each with a total capacity of 1 Mtpa, have been selected by the Department of Energy (DOE) for significant financial support from a US$3.5 billion funding pool
$85/tonne for CO2 storage in saline geologic formations from industrial and power generation facilities
note: Uncapped per-tonne credit rather than a fixed pot, so it has no headline total: US$60/t for utilisation or EOR storage, US$85/t for saline storage, rising to US$130/t and US$180/t respectively for direct air capture. Its eventual cost depends entirely on how much CO2 is actually stored — which is why it cannot be compared against a capped programme like the UK's.

programme: Canada Growth Fund — carbon contracts for difference
quote: Up to CA$7 billion of CGF’s $15 billion in capital can be allocated to CCfDs
note: A ceiling within the CA$15bn Canada Growth Fund, not a ring-fenced CCS pot: up to CA$7bn may go to carbon contracts for difference, which cover more than CCS.

awarded_note: State funding is committed to the project and largely deployed — Northern Lights began storing CO2 in 2025.
quote: the Norwegian government provided NOK 16.8 billion of the total NOK 21.1 billion capital expenditure for project Longship
note: The state carries NOK 16.8bn of a NOK 21.1bn total — roughly 80% public. Unusually for this register, the money has actually been spent and the facility is operating.

quote: a new call for proposals under the Innovation Fund, with a record budget of €4 billion for the deployment of decarbonisation technologies, including CCS and CDR
note: A single call covering decarbonisation technologies generally, with CCS and carbon removal eligible. Earlier rounds funded Northern Lights.

quote: Sweden secured approval from the Commission under the state aid rules to allocate €3 billion to support CCS projects aimed at reducing emissions from biomass combustion or processing
the first tranche of a planned 10-year, US$130 billion climate bond ... 20% is expected to be earmarked for CCS
note: DERIVED FIGURE, not a stated one: 20% of the US$130bn ten-year climate transition bond, as the report says is expected to be earmarked for CCS. The 20% is an expectation, so treat this as indicative.

quote: the government provided AU$556.1 million over 10 years for ... Geoscience Australia to comprehensively map Australia’s subsurface resources
note: Maps subsurface resources broadly, including but not limited to CO2 storage potential. It funds knowledge, not deployment — Australia has no CCS deployment pot of comparable scale in this register.
